story.title: Plague epidemic risk in Russia low after death of lab technician, WHO says
story.summary: World Health Organization detects no sign of further outbreak since Darya Shipilova died last week The World Health Organization has said the risk of an epidemic in Russia is low after the sudden death of a lab technician who worked at a plague research institute in Siberia. Darya Shipilova, who was 28, died last week, two days after falling ill. Russian media reports suggested she may have become infected after an accident at her workplace , where dangerous pathogens are kept and studied. Continue reading...

linkedin.title: Most news feeds are designed to keep you scrolling forever, but we decided to optimize for something else.
linkedin.body:
When we started building the feed for Headlinne, it would have been easy to follow the standard playbook. Most algorithms prioritize engagement metrics above all else. They want to show you whatever will keep your eyes on the screen for the longest amount of time, regardless of whether that content actually adds value to your day.

We made a different choice. Instead of optimizing for time spent, we engineered our system to prioritize signal over noise. We treat your time as a finite resource rather than a commodity to be mined. This meant building an AI model that focuses on relevance and brevity rather than just volume.

The hardest part wasn't teaching the AI to find news. The hard part was teaching it to know when to stop. We wanted to build a feed that feels like a quick, smart conversation with an editor who knows exactly what you care about, then lets you get back to your life.

It is a subtle shift in philosophy, but it changes everything about how you consume information. We believe the future of news isn't about more content. It is about better content, delivered faster.
linkedin.cta: You can see how this approach feels in practice by visiting HEADLINNE.com.

story_card.headline: OpenAI grilled over Australian government data access
story_card.standfirst: The company faced questions about how it notifies officials when its AI scrapes public

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: OpenAI admitted its handling of AI agents accessing Australian government sites was a misstep.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: In June, OpenAI agents scraped government data. The company relied on a generic email for notice.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Lawmakers want to know why OpenAI didn't contact the government directly regarding this access.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Senator David Pocock is pressing OpenAI on its notification policies during parliamentary inquiries.

story_card.caption:
OpenAI faces scrutiny after its AI agents accessed Australian government websites without direct notice.

During a parliamentary inquiry, OpenAI's chief strategy officer Jason Kwon was questioned about these events. The core issue is whether a generic department email is sufficient when AI tools interact with sensitive government data. This highlights the ongoing tension between rapid AI development and official oversight.

Should AI companies be required to get explicit permission before scraping government data?
